s0201.literal: The High Ancestor, the Grand Martial Emperor, leaned on his staff at the Tang suburb, gathered the seals of Yong and Ye, received auspicious talismans at the Cang River, and received the numinous mandate at Mount Pi.
s0201.idiomatic: The High Ancestor, the Grand Martial Emperor, took the field at Tang’s outskirts, gathered the seals of Yong and Ye, received auspicious talismans at the Cang River, and received the numinous mandate at Mount Pi.

s0202.literal: What sinks and floats, swims in foam—moving things and plants all find their source.
s0202.idiomatic: All that sink or float, all moving things and plants, drew life from that source.

s0203.literal: The Literary Emperor Taizong made a bright oath at Meng Ford and joined in descending the fire to ascend the altar;
s0203.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, the Literary Emperor, swore a bright oath at Meng Ford and, joining the descent of fire, ascended the altar;

s0204.literal: at Feng Valley he cut the serpent and, responding to massed clouds, mustered his hosts.
s0204.idiomatic: at Feng Valley he cut the serpent and, as clouds gathered, mustered his hosts.

s0205.literal: He enfeoffed at Golden Loan Ridge and displayed the great merit of successive sages;
s0205.idiomatic: He enfeoffed at Golden Loan Ridge and proclaimed the accumulated merit of the sage line;

s0206.literal: he carved stone at Wandu and fulfilled his father’s earlier intent.
s0206.idiomatic: he carved stone at Wandu and carried out his father’s long-held plan.

s0207.literal: Thus they could transform through the Bright Hall and display merit in the Grand Chamber.
s0207.idiomatic: Thus they could transform the realm through the Bright Hall and display merit in the Grand Chamber.

s0208.literal: They arrayed eight pillars on the sides and built four gates all around; carpentry needed no carving, earthworks no ornament—abundance and restraint were balanced, beginning was not rushed, what was lacking in pattern was made complete, and the great rites were thereupon perfected.
s0208.idiomatic: They arrayed eight pillars and built four gates all around; carpentry needed no carving and earthworks no ornament—abundance and restraint were balanced, the work was not rushed, pattern was completed where it had been lacking, and the great rites were perfected.

s0209.literal: The Bright Hall precinct was three hundred sixty paces on each face, with a hall placed in the center.
s0209.idiomatic: The Bright Hall precinct measured three hundred sixty paces on each side, with a hall at the center.

s0210.literal: According to the Book of Changes, the Qian tally is two hundred sixteen and the Kun tally one hundred forty-four, totaling three hundred sixty; therefore each face was three hundred sixty paces.
s0210.idiomatic: The Book of Changes gives Qian’s tally as two hundred sixteen and Kun’s as one hundred forty-four—three hundred sixty in all—so each face was made three hundred sixty paces.

s0211.literal: A hall was placed in the center, standing between the Two Modes and fixing the root of the Three Powers, constructing this one hall to oversee the ten thousand regions.
s0211.idiomatic: The central hall stood between Heaven and Earth, fixed the root of the Three Powers, and from this single structure looked out over the realm.

s0212.literal: Descending from the precinct, each face had three gates, together forming one structure, each gate-bay having five bays.
s0212.idiomatic: Below the precinct, each face had three gates forming one structure, each gate-bay spanning five bays.

s0213.literal: According to the Documents, one cycle has four seasons; therefore on each face one gate-opening was set;
s0213.idiomatic: The Documents say one cycle has four seasons, so each face had one gate-opening;

s0214.literal: each season has three months, so each opening had three gates;
s0214.idiomatic: with three months per season, each opening received three gates;

s0215.literal: one cycle has twelve months, so in all there were twelve gates around.
s0215.idiomatic: and one cycle has twelve months, for twelve gates in all around the precinct.

s0216.literal: Thus one gate on each face answered the four seasons; since one season governs three months, three gates were placed in one gate-structure.
s0216.idiomatic: One gate per face matched the four seasons; because one season governs three months, three gates were set in each gate-structure.

s0217.literal: Again, in the Book of Changes three is the yang number and two the yin number; together they make five—hence each gate-structure had five bays.
s0217.idiomatic: In the Book of Changes, three is yang and two is yin—five together—so each gate-structure had five bays.

s0218.literal: At the four corners of the precinct double towers were set, and each enclosing wall followed its direction’s color.
s0218.idiomatic: At the four corners stood double towers, and each enclosing wall took the color of its direction.

s0219.literal: According to the Huainanzi, the earth has four corners; hence four towers.
s0219.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says the earth has four corners—hence four towers.

s0220.literal: Again, according to the Monthly Ordinances, the five directions—water, fire, metal, wood, and earth—each has a distinct color; therefore each wall followed its direction’s color.
s0220.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances assign distinct colors to water, fire, metal, wood, and earth—so each wall followed its direction’s color.

s0221.literal: The base had eight faces, symbolizing the eight directions.
s0221.idiomatic: The base was octagonal, symbolizing the eight directions.

s0222.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, “the yellow jade cube sacrifices to Earth.”
s0222.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou say, “the yellow jade cube sacrifices to Earth.”

s0223.literal: Zheng Xuan’s commentary: the cube is jade of the eight directions, symbolizing earth’s form; therefore it sacrifices to Earth.
s0223.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: the cube is jade of the eight directions, symbolizing earth’s form, and thus sacrifices to Earth.

s0224.literal: From this one knows the terrain has eight directions.
s0224.idiomatic: Hence the terrain has eight directions.

s0225.literal: Again, according to the History of Han, Emperor Wu established the Eight Gu altars to sacrifice to Earth.
s0225.idiomatic: The History of Han says Emperor Wu built the Eight Gu altars to sacrifice to Earth.

s0226.literal: Ascending the altar to Earth symbolizes earth’s form; therefore the base was made with eight faces to symbolize the terrain.
s0226.idiomatic: The altar to Earth symbolizes earth’s form, so the base was made octagonal to match the terrain.

s0227.literal: The base was one zhang two chi high and two hundred eighty chi in diameter.
s0227.idiomatic: The base stood one zhang two chi high and two hundred eighty chi across.

s0228.literal: According to the History of Han, yang is the six pitch-pipes and yin the six secondary pipes.
s0228.idiomatic: The History of Han treats yang as the six pitch-pipes and yin as the six secondary pipes.

s0229.literal: Yang and yin join; therefore the height is one zhang two chi.
s0229.idiomatic: Yang and yin join—hence the height of one zhang two chi.

s0230.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, three is the yang number and eight the yin number.
s0230.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes three yang and eight yin.

s0231.literal: Three and eight multiplied yield two hundred forty chi.
s0231.idiomatic: Three times eight gives two hundred forty chi.

s0232.literal: According to the History of Han, the nine conjunctions’ tally has forty; together they make two hundred eighty—hence the base diameter of two hundred eighty chi.
s0232.idiomatic: The History of Han’s tally of nine conjunctions adds forty to two hundred forty—two hundred eighty—fixing the base diameter.

s0233.literal: Thus Heaven and Earth’s harmonies were joined and yin-yang numbers interwoven.
s0233.idiomatic: So Heaven and Earth’s harmonies met and yin-yang numbers were woven together.

s0234.literal: To show yang does not move alone but borrows yin’s harmony to complete its work;
s0234.idiomatic: Yang does not move alone but borrows yin’s harmony to finish its work;

s0235.literal: yin does not proceed alone but waits for yang’s lead before responding.
s0235.idiomatic: yin does not act alone but waits for yang’s lead before answering.

s0236.literal: When yin and yang both accord and Heaven and Earth are all penetrating, the hundred treasures arise and the nine categories are ordered.
s0236.idiomatic: When yin and yang accord and Heaven and Earth penetrate, the hundred treasures arise and the nine categories fall into order.

s0237.literal: Each face of the base had three steps, twelve steps around, each step having twenty-five treads.
s0237.idiomatic: Each face of the base had three steps—twelve around—with twenty-five treads per step.

s0238.literal: According to the History of Han, Heaven has three steps; therefore three steps on each face;
s0238.idiomatic: The History of Han says Heaven has three steps—hence three steps on each face;

s0239.literal: Earth has the twelve chronograms; therefore twelve steps around.
s0239.idiomatic: Earth has the twelve chronograms—hence twelve steps around.

s0240.literal: Again, according to the Wenzi, from the common to the sage there are twenty-five grades; therefore twenty-five treads per step.
s0240.idiomatic: The Wenzi counts twenty-five grades from commoner to sage—hence twenty-five treads per step.

s0241.literal: Thus steps answered the asterisms and patterned the terrace’s glory in the steps, above matching the azure vault’s rites and below following the earthly chronograms’ numbers.
s0241.idiomatic: Steps matched the asterisms and patterned the terrace’s glory, above echoing the azure vault and below the earthly chronograms.

s0242.literal: These repeated grades also measured sage against commoner.
s0242.idiomatic: The graded steps also measured sage against commoner.

s0243.literal: They symbolized the august pole’s high dwelling, looking down on the myriad kinds in radiance.
s0243.idiomatic: They symbolized the august pole’s height, looking down on all creatures in radiance.

s0244.literal: Above the base stood a single hall, its roof-space round above.
s0244.idiomatic: Above the base stood one hall with a round upper roof-space.

s0245.literal: According to the Classic of the Way and Its Power: Heaven obtaining One becomes clear, Earth obtaining One becomes tranquil, and lords obtaining One become the world’s standard.
s0245.idiomatic: The Classic of the Way says Heaven with One grows clear, Earth with One grows still, and rulers with One become the world’s standard.

s0246.literal: It also says: the Way gives birth to One; One gives birth to Two; Two gives birth to Three; Three gives birth to the ten thousand things.
s0246.idiomatic: It also says: the Way begets One; One begets Two; Two begets Three; Three begets the ten thousand things.

s0247.literal: Again, according to the History of Han: the Grand Ultimate’s primordial qi enfolds three as one.
s0247.idiomatic: The History of Han says the Grand Ultimate’s primordial qi enfolds three as one.

s0248.literal: It also says: the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his house.
s0248.idiomatic: It also says the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his house.

s0249.literal: Therefore one hall was set to symbolize primordial qi and also to take the meaning of the four seas as home.
s0249.idiomatic: Hence one hall symbolized primordial qi and the four seas as home.

s0250.literal: Again, according to the Rites of Zhou, “the green jade disc sacrifices to Heaven.”
s0250.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou say, “the green jade disc sacrifices to Heaven.”

s0251.literal: Zheng Xuan’s commentary: the disc is round to symbolize Heaven.
s0251.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: the disc is round to symbolize Heaven.

s0252.literal: Therefore the roof-space was made round above.
s0252.idiomatic: Hence the upper roof-space was round.

s0253.literal: Each face of the hall had nine bays, each bay one zhang nine chi wide.
s0253.idiomatic: Each face of the hall had nine bays, each one zhang nine chi wide.

s0254.literal: According to the Documents, Earth has nine regions; therefore nine bays were set.
s0254.idiomatic: The Documents say Earth has nine regions—hence nine bays.

s0255.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, ten is the yin number; therefore each bay was one zhang nine chi wide—thus patterning the thick earth, taking yin-yang as standard, joining the two qi through the base, and placing the nine regions in one hall.
s0255.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes ten yin—hence bays of one zhang nine chi, patterning the thick earth, fixing yin-yang, joining the two qi at the base, and gathering the nine regions in one hall.

s0256.literal: Twelve gates went around the hall; each gate was one zhang seven chi high and one zhang three chi wide.
s0256.idiomatic: Twelve gates encircled the hall, each one zhang seven chi high and one zhang three chi wide.

s0257.literal: According to the Record of Rites, one year has twelve months; therefore twelve gates were set.
s0257.idiomatic: The Record of Rites gives twelve months in a year—hence twelve gates.

s0258.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, ten is the yin number and seven the yang number; therefore the height is one zhang seven chi;
s0258.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes ten yin and seven yang—hence height of one zhang seven chi;

s0259.literal: it also says five is yang and eight yin; therefore the width is one zhang three chi.
s0259.idiomatic: five yang and eight yin fix the width at one zhang three chi.

s0260.literal: Thus the jade candle was tuned and the golden splendor answered; the two qi turned in cycle and the four seasons were welcomed in turn.
s0260.idiomatic: Thus the jade candle was tuned, golden splendor answered, the two qi cycled, and the four seasons were welcomed in turn.

s0261.literal: Twenty-four windows went around the hall, each one zhang three chi high and one zhang one chi wide, with twenty-three lattice-bars and twenty-four lights.
s0261.idiomatic: Twenty-four windows encircled the hall, each one zhang three chi high and one zhang one chi wide, with twenty-three lattice-bars and twenty-four lights.

s0262.literal: According to the Records of the Historian, Heaven has twenty-four qi; therefore twenty-four windows were set.
s0262.idiomatic: The Records say Heaven has twenty-four qi—hence twenty-four windows.

s0263.literal: Again, according to the Documents, twelve months in a year, including the intercalation, symbolized in the height of one zhang three chi.
s0263.idiomatic: The Documents’ twelve months plus intercalation are echoed in the height of one zhang three chi.

s0264.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, Heaven’s number is one and Earth’s ten; therefore the width is one zhang one chi;
s0264.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes Heaven one and Earth ten—width one zhang one chi;

s0265.literal: Heaven’s number nine and Earth’s ten, with the four seasons making twenty-three, yield twenty-three lattice-bars.
s0265.idiomatic: nine and ten with the four seasons yield twenty-three lattice-bars.

s0266.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, the eight pure hexagrams in their basic bodies, totaling twenty-four lines, give twenty-four lights.
s0266.idiomatic: The eight pure hexagrams’ twenty-four lines give twenty-four lights.

s0267.literal: Windows ranged in rows, symbolizing wind and seasonal qi, broadly encompassing Heaven and Earth’s numbers and closely matching yin-yang’s harmony.
s0267.idiomatic: Ranked windows symbolized wind and seasonal qi, spanning Heaven and Earth’s numbers and matching yin-yang’s harmony.

s0268.literal: At the hall’s center were eight pillars, each fifty-five chi long.
s0268.idiomatic: Eight pillars stood at the hall’s center, each fifty-five chi tall.

s0269.literal: According to the River Chart, eight pillars bear Heaven; therefore eight pillars were set.
s0269.idiomatic: The River Chart says eight pillars bear Heaven—hence eight pillars.

s0270.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, the Great Expansion’s number is fifty-five; therefore the length is fifty-five chi.
s0270.idiomatic: The Book of Changes’ Great Expansion number is fifty-five—hence fifty-five chi.

s0271.literal: These eight pillars rose to bear the nine bays—number matching the Great Expansion’s rule, form matching the established pole’s design.
s0271.idiomatic: Eight pillars rose to bear nine bays—number matching Great Expansion, form matching the established pole.

s0272.literal: Moreover pillars are yin in number while Heaven is truly yang in origin; pillars rise by yin qi while Heaven descends by yang harmony—thus yin and yang interchange and Heaven and Earth succeed each other.
s0272.idiomatic: Pillars are yin in number while Heaven is yang in origin; pillars rise on yin qi as Heaven descends in yang harmony—yin and yang interchange and Heaven and Earth succeed each other.

s0273.literal: Outside the hall’s center, four pillars were set as the Four Assistants.
s0273.idiomatic: Outside the central eight pillars stood four more as the Four Assistants.

s0274.literal: According to the History of Han, Heaven has four Assistant stars; therefore four pillars were set to symbolize the four stars.
s0274.idiomatic: The History of Han names four Assistant stars—hence four pillars symbolizing them.

s0275.literal: Within, eight pillars bore Heaven; without, four Assistants displayed transformation—above communicating, below penetrating, inner and outer completing each other, matching the terrace’s glory in divided radiance and stringing pearls to embrace the pole.
s0275.idiomatic: Eight pillars bore Heaven within; four Assistants displayed transformation without—above and below in communication, inner and outer complete, sharing the terrace’s glory and stringing pearls around the pole.

s0276.literal: Beyond the eight pillars and four Assistants, the first ring had twenty pillars.
s0276.idiomatic: Outside the eight pillars and four Assistants, the first ring held twenty pillars.

s0277.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Heaven’s number five and Earth’s ten, together with the Five Phases’ number, total twenty; therefore twenty pillars were set.
s0277.idiomatic: Heaven’s five, Earth’s ten, and the Five Phases make twenty—hence twenty pillars.

s0278.literal: Embodying the Two Modes in number, matching the Five Positions in measure, conforming to the established pole’s achievement, and truly answering the way of firm and yielding.
s0278.idiomatic: They embodied the Two Modes in number, the Five Positions in measure, the established pole’s work, and the way of firm and yielding.

s0279.literal: Beyond the eight pillars and four Assistants, the second ring had twenty-eight pillars.
s0279.idiomatic: Beyond them, the second ring had twenty-eight pillars.

s0280.literal: According to the Records of the Historian, Heaven has twenty-eight lodges; therefore twenty-eight pillars.
s0280.idiomatic: The Records say Heaven has twenty-eight lodges—hence twenty-eight pillars.

s0281.literal: Thus looking up one matches the Qian chart, above matching the bright lodges, examining strung pearls to record degrees, and observing the lodges to welcome the seasons.
s0281.idiomatic: Looking up, one matches the Qian chart and the bright lodges, strings pearls to mark degrees, and watches the lodges to welcome the seasons.

s0282.literal: Beyond the eight pillars and four Assistants, the third ring had thirty-two pillars.
s0282.idiomatic: The third ring had thirty-two pillars.

s0283.literal: According to the History of Han, there are eight nodes, eight policies, eight winds, and eight sounds—four eights make thirty-two pillars.
s0283.idiomatic: The History of Han lists eight nodes, eight policies, eight winds, and eight sounds—four eights, thirty-two pillars.

s0284.literal: Regulating wind and governing the seasons, the ten thousand things borrow this to transform and grow;
s0284.idiomatic: Regulating wind and seasons, the ten thousand things borrow this to grow;

s0285.literal: spreading government and flowing music, the nine regions look up and take it as model.
s0285.idiomatic: spreading government and music, the nine regions look up and take it as model.

s0286.literal: On the outside, thirty-six pillars went all around.
s0286.idiomatic: Outside, thirty-six pillars ran all around.

s0287.literal: According to the History of Han, one cycle has thirty-six ten-day weeks; therefore thirty-six pillars were patterned on this.
s0287.idiomatic: One cycle has thirty-six ten-day weeks—hence thirty-six outer pillars.

s0288.literal: Thus the seasons were symbolized for use, cold and heat followed in subtle accord, the armillary’s measure was without error, and the jade calendar’s term was ever in covenant.
s0288.idiomatic: They symbolized the seasons for use, followed cold and heat in subtle accord, kept the armillary without error, and matched the jade calendar’s term.

s0289.literal: Beyond the eight pillars, heights and lengths totaled three grades.
s0289.idiomatic: Beyond the eight pillars, pillar heights fell into three grades.

s0290.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Heaven, Earth, and Man are the Three Powers; therefore three grades of pillar length.
s0290.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and Man are the Three Powers—hence three grades of length.

s0291.literal: Thus the Three Powers were imitated for position, high and low contrasting;
s0291.idiomatic: Thus the Three Powers fixed position, high and low contrasting;

s0292.literal: the ten thousand things were embodied for nurture, long and short both employed.
s0292.idiomatic: the ten thousand things were nurtured, long and short both employed.

s0293.literal: Beyond the eight pillars, the total was one hundred twenty pillars.
s0293.idiomatic: Beyond the eight pillars, pillars totaled one hundred twenty.

s0294.literal: According to the Record of Rites, the Son of Heaven appoints three dukes, nine ministers, twenty-seven grand masters, and eighty-one elemental officers—totaling one hundred twenty; therefore one hundred twenty pillars were set.
s0294.idiomatic: The Record of Rites counts three dukes, nine ministers, twenty-seven grand masters, and eighty-one elemental officers—one hundred twenty—hence one hundred twenty pillars.

s0295.literal: Dividing offices and setting officials, aiding transformation relies on many scholars;
s0295.idiomatic: Offices divided and officials set, transformation relies on many scholars;

s0296.literal: opening things and accomplishing tasks, building the spring hall borrows the host of talents.
s0296.idiomatic: opening things and accomplishing tasks, the spring hall rests on a host of talents.

s0297.literal: Above them the railing-courses went around in two hundred fourteen.
s0297.idiomatic: Above, railing-courses ran two hundred fourteen around.

s0298.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Kun’s tally is one hundred forty-four; again, the History of Han’s nine conjunctions’ tally has sixty—therefore two hundred fourteen railing-courses.
s0298.idiomatic: Kun’s tally is one hundred forty-four and the History of Han’s nine conjunctions add sixty—two hundred fourteen railing-courses.

s0299.literal: Thus Kun’s tally’s subtle mystery was taken, the jia-yi cycle’s refinement was patterned, circling to match the asterisms’ rule and structuring to match yin-yang’s numbers.
s0299.idiomatic: They took Kun’s subtle tally, patterned the jia-yi refinement, circled to match the asterisms, and structured to yin-yang’s numbers.

s0300.literal: Again, because the base symbolizes Earth, the tally was applied to Kun’s origin;
s0300.idiomatic: Because the base symbolizes Earth, the tally was applied to Kun’s origin;
